hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: Precompute remaining suffix frequencies of every number in the array.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: The highest achievable mex of any prefix of the remaining suffix is the suffix mex.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Greedily slice the shortest prefix containing all values from 0 to mex minus 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import Counter

def maxMexArray(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(nums)
    rem_counts = Counter(nums)
    res = []
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        mex = 0
        while rem_counts[mex] > 0:
            mex += 1
        if mex == 0:
            res.extend([0] * (n - i))
            break
        needed = set(range(mex))
        seen = set()
        j = i
        while j < n and needed:
            val = nums[j]
            rem_counts[val] -= 1
            if val in needed:
                seen.add(val)
                if len(seen) == mex:
                    j += 1
                    break
            j += 1
        res.append(mex)
        i = j
    return res
```

complexity.notes: Each element is processed a constant number of times during greedy MEX prefix extraction.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all possible partition cuts results in exponential combinations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identifies that greedy choice of maximal suffix MEX produces the lexicographically greatest sequence.
